indices.label: Market Deal Momentum
indices.blurb: Market Deal Momentum holds in the 55-65 range across the catalog, with large-deal traction concentrated in three pockets: GenAI managed-services transformations, sovereign-cloud public-sector contracts, and platform-engineering renewals at BFSI accounts. Indian engineering specialists (Coforge, Persistent, LTTS) lead bookings growth on a percentage basis, while global SIs anchor absolute TCV. Booking-to-revenue lag is widening — visible AI bookings are not yet flowing into recognized services revenue at the pace investor narratives imply.

indices.label: Market Reputation Index
indices.blurb: Reputation index holds steady against H2 2025 — averaging mid-60s across the catalog with notable bifurcation: tier-1 brand strength insulates Accenture, Capgemini, and Cognizant from broader sentiment softness, while CX/BPO providers face employee-side reputation drag from AI-displacement messaging. Customer-side scores on G2/Capterra hold firm; employee-side scores on Glassdoor and Blind show the largest negative deltas for providers in active restructuring.

indices.label: Market AI Disruption Risk
indices.blurb: AI Disruption Risk averages 38 across the catalog (lower is better — the index inverts AI readiness), with CX/Contact Center BPO segments at the high-risk end and Digital Engineering specialists at the low-risk end. Concentrix, Teleperformance, and Atento face the steepest near-term displacement risk from conversational AI deployments on the customer side. Global SIs sit in the middle band — internal AI tooling is mature, but client AI projects also threaten to compress historical fee structures over 2026-2027.

indices.label: Market Headwinds
indices.blurb: The composite Headwind score sits in the upper-50s catalog-wide, driven by FX exposure (rupee/euro/sterling volatility against USD reporting) and lingering client concentration in financial services. Headwinds are highest for Indian providers with single-customer revenue concentration above 10% and lowest for diversified European SIs. Macro indicators suggest headwinds peak in calendar Q3 before easing as enterprise discretionary IT spend recovers.
